nodes.title: Skolem data, completeness, and integral points (Moret-Bailly II 1.1-1.2, 1.5, 1.8)
nodes.statement: Let R be a Dedekind ring which is either the ring of S-integers of a number field (arithmetic case) or the ring of a smooth connected affine curve over a finite field (geometric case); K = Frac(R), B = Spec R. Let f: X -> B be separated of finite type with f surjective, X_K geometrically irreducible over K, and X irreducible. Let Sigma be a finite set of places of K (archimedean or not) disjoint from Max(R), the closed points of B viewed as places. For v in Sigma fix a finite Galois extension L_v of the completion K_v and a nonempty open subset Omega_v of X(L_v) for the v-topology, consisting of smooth points and stable under Gal(L_v/K_v). The sequence S = (f: X -> B, Sigma, {L_v}, {Omega_v}) is a Skolem datum; it is complete if every place of K lies in Sigma or in Max(R), and incomplete otherwise. An integral point of S is an irreducible closed subscheme Y of X, finite and surjective over B, such that for every v in Sigma the scheme Y tensor_R L_v is L_v-split (made of L_v-rational points) and contained in Omega_v. Equivalently (Remarque 1.5): Y_K = Spec K' for a finite extension K'/K, the inclusion gives x in X(R') with R' the normalisation of R in K', K' tensor_K K_v is a product of copies of L_v, and every embedding K' -> L_v maps x into Omega_v.
hypotheses: R is the ring of S-integers of a number field or the ring of a smooth connected affine curve over a finite field (Remarque 1.7 extends Théorème 1.3 to any localisation of the ring of integers of a number field or of the ring of a curve over a finite field, by spreading X out)
f separated of finite type and surjective; X irreducible; X_K geometrically irreducible over K
Sigma finite and disjoint from Max(R); each L_v/K_v finite Galois; each Omega_v nonempty, v-adically open, made of smooth points and Gal(L_v/K_v)-stable
incompleteness (some place of K outside Sigma and outside Max(R)) is essential: Remarque 1.8 gives a complete datum without integral point
proofSteps: 1.1 and Définition 1.2 fix the data and the notion of integral point; the displayed local conditions (Sigma, Omega_v, L_v-split) were read on the page image of p. 181 because the OCR drops Sigma and Omega.

Remarque 1.5 reads an integral point as a finite extension K'/K in which each v in Sigma decomposes as a product of copies of L_v, together with an R'-integral point of X lying in Omega_v at every embedding K' -> L_v; it notes that this generalises the Cantor-Roquette density theorem (essentially X_K unirational and L_v = K_v).
Remarque 1.8: R = Z, X = G_m over Z, Sigma = {ordinary absolute value}, L = C, Omega = {|z| < 1} is a complete Skolem datum without integral point; the source only says this is immediate.
acceptance: For K = Q, R = Z[1/N] and Sigma = {infinity} with L_infinity = R and Omega_infinity = X(R): check that an integral point is exactly a totally real field K' with an R'-point, as used later to produce totally real fields

nodes.title: Density of separable and algebraic points in local point sets (Lemme 1.6.1, Corollaire 1.6.2, Lemme 2.1)
nodes.statement: (Lemme 1.6.1) Let F be a local field, F-bar an algebraic closure, F^s the separable closure of F in F-bar, and X an F-scheme of finite type which is generically smooth over F. Then X(F^s) is dense in X(F-bar) for the valuation topology. (Corollaire 1.6.2) Let F be a non-archimedean local field with ring of integers A and let 𝔛 be an A-scheme of finite type, flat and surjective over A, whose generic fibre is generically smooth over F. Then there is a finite separable extension F'/F with ring of integers A' such that 𝔛(A') is nonempty. (Lemme 2.1) Let F be a field with a discrete valuation v, F-hat its completion and F' the algebraic closure of F in F-hat, and assume F-hat is separable over F (i.e. the valuation ring is excellent). Then for every F-scheme Z of finite type, Z(F') is dense in Z(F-hat) for the v-topology.
hypotheses: Lemme 1.6.1: F a local field; X of finite type and generically smooth over F; in characteristic 0 the statement is empty
Corollaire 1.6.2: F non-archimedean; 𝔛 flat and surjective over A; generic fibre generically smooth
Lemme 2.1: F-hat separable over F (excellent valuation ring); the author states he does not know whether this hypothesis is superfluous
proofSteps: 1.6.1(a), X = affine line, char F = p > 0: for x in F-bar with v(x) >= 0 pick k with x^(p^k) = a in F^s; for n >= 1 let y_n be a root of y^(p^k) - t^n y - a = 0 with t a uniformiser of F; then y_n is in F^s, v(y_n) >= 0 and v(y_n - x) = p^(-k) v(y_n^(p^k) - a) = p^(-k) v(t^n y_n) >= n p^(-k) (display read on the page image of p. 183).

1.6.1(b), general case: reduce to X smooth; near the closed point P under x choose a Zariski open U and an F-morphism U -> A^n (n = dim X) finite étale over a neighbourhood of the image of P; it induces a homeomorphism of a neighbourhood of x onto an open of F-bar^n, and a point is F^s-rational iff its image is, because the map is étale; conclude by (a).
1.6.2: with A^s, A-bar the integers of F^s, F-bar, one has 𝔛(A^s) = 𝔛(A-bar) ∩ 𝔛(F^s), and 𝔛(A-bar) is a nonempty open of 𝔛(F-bar) because 𝔛 is flat and surjective over A; apply 1.6.1.

2.1: clear for affine space; in general stratify Z into regular locally closed pieces, note that an F-hat-point factors through the smooth locus, shrink to an étale map Z -> U with U open in affine space, take an F'-point of the (open) image of a given open set and use that fibres of the quasi-finite map consist of points algebraic over F.

nodes.title: Elementary reductions: quasi-projective, shrinking X_K, enlarging Sigma (Remarques 1.4, 1.9, 1.10, Exemple 1.10.1)
nodes.statement: To prove Théorème 1.3 one may assume: (1.4) f quasi-projective, by Chow's lemma (EGA II 5.6); (1.9) X_K smooth: if F_K is a strict closed subset of X_K with closure F in X, then F contains no fibre of f (the closed fibres of f are purely of codimension 1), X - F -> B is still surjective, F(L_v) does not contain Omega_v (the latter is an L_v-analytic manifold of dimension dim X_K > dim F_K), and (X - F -> B, {L_v}, {Omega_v - F(L_v)}) is again a Skolem datum; (1.10) Sigma may be enlarged by a finite set S of closed points of B: B_1 = B - S is affine because Pic(B) = Cl(R) is finite, for v in S Corollaire 1.6.2 gives a finite Galois L_v/K_v with integers R'_v such that Omega_v := X(R'_v) is a nonempty Galois-stable open of X(L_v), the datum S_1 = (X_1 = X x_B B_1 -> B_1, Sigma ∪ S, {L_v}, {Omega_v}) is a Skolem datum, and the closure in X of an integral point of S_1 is an integral point of S. (1.10.1) Consequently X may be replaced by any nonempty open subscheme, e.g. X smooth over B.

nodes.title: Reduction to relative dimension one by Bertini hypersurface sections (Lemmes 2.2-2.3, 2.4)
nodes.statement: Assume f quasi-projective and X_K smooth. (Lemme 2.2) There is a closed subset T of X of dimension 1, quasi-finite and surjective over B, meeting every Omega_v in the sense that T(L_v) ∩ Omega_v is nonempty for all v in Sigma. (Lemme 2.3) If dim X_K = n >= 2, there is a hypersurface X'_K of X_K, geometrically irreducible, containing T_K and regular at the points of T_K. (2.4) With X' the closure of X'_K in X and Omega'_v = {smooth points of X'_K(L_v)} ∩ Omega_v, the datum S' = (X' -> B, Sigma, {L_v}, {Omega'_v}) is a Skolem datum, incomplete if S is, with dim X'_K = dim X_K - 1, and the image in X of an integral point of S' is an integral point of S. By induction one reduces Théorème 1.3 to dim X_K = 1.
hypotheses: f quasi-projective (Remarque 1.4) and X_K smooth over K (Remarque 1.9)
incompleteness is not needed for this reduction (the source says so explicitly before Lemme 2.2)
Bertini's theorem is imported: Jouanolou, Théorèmes de Bertini et applications, chapter I, theorem 6.3
proofSteps: Lemme 2.2: by Lemme 2.1 each Omega_v contains a point algebraic over K, i.e. lying over a closed point P_v of X_K; the closure T_v of P_v is quasi-finite over B; the union of the T_v maps onto B minus a finite set S of closed points; for each v in S add a closed T_v quasi-finite over B whose image contains v.

Lemme 2.3: embed X_K in P^N, let L_d be the linear system of degree-d hypersurface sections containing T_K; for d large L_d embeds the blow-up of X-bar_K along T_K, so Bertini gives a dense open U_d of geometrically irreducible members; for d large H^1(X-bar_K, I.I_x(d)) = 0 for x in T_K gives a dense open V_d of members regular at T_K; choose s in (U_d ∩ V_d)(K).

2.4: X' is irreducible with geometrically irreducible generic fibre and contains T, hence is surjective over B; for v in Sigma a point t_v in T_K(L_v) ∩ Omega_v has residue field inside L_v, hence separable over K, so X'_K is smooth there and Omega'_v is a nonempty open; induct on dim X_K (if dim X_K = 0 then f is an isomorphism).

nodes.title: Curve case set-up: generalized Picard functor PG(X̄, Z) and the affine-space fibration of effective divisors (3.1-3.6)
nodes.statement: Let S = (f: X -> B, Sigma, {L_v}, {Omega_v}) be a Skolem datum with dim X_K = 1 and f quasi-projective and smooth. Choose a compactification j: X -> X-bar over B with f-bar projective and X-bar normal; Z = X-bar - X with its reduced structure; g = h^1(X-bar_K, O) and z = deg_K(Z_K), with z > 0 after enlarging Z. After shrinking B and enlarging Sigma (1.10): (3.1.2) X-bar is regular, the fibres of f-bar are geometrically integral, and Z is regular and finite, flat and surjective over B (so a Cartier divisor). For d in N the symmetric power X^(d) = X^d/S_d (fibre product over B) represents effective Cartier divisors of X-bar_S finite flat of degree d over S and disjoint from Z; U_d ⊂ X^(d) is the open of étale divisors; Omega_v^[d] ⊂ U_d(K_v) is the set of effective étale divisors of degree d on X ⊗ K_v which are L_v-split and contained in Omega_v. PG(X-bar, Z)(S) (resp. PG_d) is the group of isomorphism classes of pairs (line bundle L on X-bar_S, trivialisation of L on Z_S) (resp. with L of degree d); there is an exact sequence of sheaves 1 -> G_m,B -> (pi_Z)_* G_m,Z -> PG(X-bar, Z) -> Pic_{X-bar/B} -> 1, and PG(X-bar, Z) is represented by a smooth separated group scheme locally of finite presentation (only the representability of its generic fibre, from Murre's theorem, SGA 6 XII 1.5, is used). The map phi_d: X^(d) -> PG_d, D -> cl^Z(D) = class of (O(D), s_D restricted to Z), has fibres described by (3.5.4). Lemme 3.3: Omega_v^[d] is open in U_d(K_v) for all d >= 0, and nonempty if [L_v : K_v] divides d. Lemme 3.6: if d >= 2g + z - 1, phi_d is a locally trivial fibration in affine spaces of dimension d + 1 - g - z.
hypotheses: dim X_K = 1, f quasi-projective and smooth (reached by 1.4, 1.9, 1.10 and section 2)
normalisation of X-bar keeps X unchanged because X is regular (f smooth)
(3.1.2) is achieved only after replacing B by an open subscheme and enlarging Sigma; it cites EGA IV 12.2.1 for geometric integrality of fibres
the inequality in Lemme 3.6 is d >= 2g + z - 1 (checked on page image p. 189; the OCR prints it garbled)
the duality argument of 3.6 uses that X-bar is regular hence Gorenstein and that each fibre X-bar_b is geometrically reduced
proofSteps: 3.2: the projection X^d -> X^(d) is étale off the diagonals; (3.2.3) identifies X^(d)(S) with effective Cartier divisors finite flat of degree d over S and disjoint from Z (X smooth over B).

Lemme 3.3(i): Omega_v^[d] = Omega' ∩ U_d(K_v) where Omega' is the image of Omega_v^d minus diagonals under an étale projection, hence open. (ii): with delta = [L_v : K_v] and d = r delta, the union of the proper intermediate analytic submanifolds Omega_v ∩ X(M) has empty interior, so there are r points of degree delta over K_v, pairwise non-conjugate, whose conjugates form a K_v-rational divisor in Omega_v^[d].

3.4: rigidity of the categories of pairs (from 3.1.2(ii) and surjectivity of Z -> B) makes PG sheaves; (3.4.2) exhibits PG(X-bar, Z) as an extension of Pic by the smooth affine group (pi_Z)_* G_m,Z / G_m,B.
3.5: a section s of L with s|Z = alpha is regular, and div(s) is in X^(d)(S); this gives the bijection (3.5.4) between X^(d)(S) and triples (L, alpha, s).

Lemme 3.6: for d >= 2g + z - 1, R^1 pr_2* of the universal bundle and of its twist by -Z vanish by duality; so the direct images E_d, N_d commute with base change and the restriction r_d: E_d -> F_d is a surjection of locally free sheaves with kernel N_d; the subscheme r_d^(-1)(Im sigma_d) of V(E_d-dual) is U^(d)... identified with X^(d) over P_d, a torsor under the vector bundle V(N_d-dual) of rank d + 1 - g - z.

nodes.title: Taylor's Theorem G: points over the maximal extension split at S are Zariski dense
nodes.statement: (Taylor, Theorem G, attributed to Moret-Bailly [M] = part II) Let K be a number field and S a finite set of places of K; let K_S be the unique maximal extension of K inside a fixed algebraic closure in which all places of S split completely (for K = Q and S = {infinity}, K_S is the maximal totally real field). If X/Spec K is a geometrically irreducible smooth quasi-projective scheme with X(K_v) nonempty for all v in S, then X(K_S) is Zariski dense in X. KW II (proof of Theorem 6.1) uses the stronger form with open sets: applying Théorème 1.3 with prescribed v-adic open subsets Omega_v of local points (for example the points of X(Q_p) reducing to a given integral point x_v) yields a point over a field split at the given places whose local images lie in Omega_v.
hypotheses: K a number field; S finite; X geometrically irreducible, smooth and quasi-projective over K; X(K_v) nonempty for every v in S
the conclusion concerns K_S, an infinite extension; a single point lies over a finite subextension K' ⊂ K_S, which need not be Galois over K

neither Taylor nor Moret-Bailly II writes out the deduction of Theorem G from Théorème 1.3 (spreading X out over O_K[1/N] with N divisible by a prime not in S, taking L_v = K_v and Omega_v = X(K_v) ∩ U(K_v) for Zariski opens U); this deduction is recorded as a gap
proofSteps: Taylor recalls Theorem G in the introduction and applies it in section 1 with S = places above l, p and infinity; no proof is given in Taylor.

Intended deduction (not written in the sources read): let S' be a finite set of places of K containing S, the archimedean places, one finite place v_0 not in S and the places of bad behaviour of a chosen model; let R be the ring of S'-integers and spread X out to an irreducible separated finite-type R-scheme, surjective over Spec R after enlarging S'; put Sigma = S, which is disjoint from Max(R) and leaves v_0 outside Sigma ∪ Max(R) (incomplete datum); take L_v = K_v and Omega_v = X(K_v) ∩ U(K_v) for a nonempty Zariski open U of X_K (nonempty by the analytic-dimension argument of Remarque 1.9, since X is smooth and X(K_v) is nonempty); Théorème 1.3 and Remarque 1.5 give K' with K' ⊗_K K_v a product of copies of K_v for v in S, i.e. K' ⊂ K_S, and a point of U(K').

nodes.title: Forcing linear disjointness from a given finite extension by extra split places
nodes.statement: (KW II, proof of Theorem 6.1(iii)(d)) Given a finite extension L of Q, one can impose that the totally real field F produced by the Moret-Bailly theorem is linearly disjoint from L: when applying the theorem one additionally requires F to be split at a chosen finite set of primes which are unramified in L and whose Frobenius elements generate the Galois group of the Galois closure of L/Q, chosen disjoint from the primes above p and the auxiliary primes so that all local conditions can be imposed simultaneously. KW Annals (proof of Theorem 2.1) uses this to get im(rho-bar) = im(rho-bar|G_F), by taking L the fixed field of ker(rho-bar), and cites for the same refinement Proposition 2.1 of Harris-Shepherd-Barron-Taylor.
hypotheses: the added primes must be unramified in L and distinct from p and from the auxiliary primes of the moduli problem
their Frobenius elements must generate Gal(L~/Q), L~ the Galois closure of L/Q (Chebotarev supplies such primes; not stated in the source)

the deduction 'F split at primes whose Frobenii generate Gal(L~/Q) implies F ∩ L~ = Q, hence F and L~ (so F and L) linearly disjoint' is not written in KW II; it is the standard argument that every generator lies in Gal(L~/(F ∩ L~)) because each such prime splits completely in F ∩ L~
proofSteps: Add the chosen primes q_1, ..., q_m to Sigma with L_{q_i} = Q_{q_i} and Omega_{q_i} = X(Q_{q_i}) (nonempty local points must be checked for the moduli space at these primes; KW II does not discuss this point).
A field F split completely at each q_i has F ∩ L~ split completely at each q_i, so Frob_{q_i} fixes F ∩ L~; these generate Gal(L~/Q), hence F ∩ L~ = Q.
Since L~/Q is Galois, F ∩ L~ = Q implies F and L~ are linearly disjoint, hence also F and L.

nodes.statement: Standing hypotheses of Taylor 2002 section 1 as corrected in Taylor 2006 (pp. 776-777): l an odd prime, k/F_l finite, F totally real, rho-bar: G_F -> GL_2(k) continuous with insoluble image, rho-bar|G_v ~ (epsilon chi_v^{-1}, *; 0, chi_v) for every place v of F above l, and det rho-bar = epsilon (the corrected third bullet; epsilon the l-adic cyclotomic character mod l). For v | l let F~_v be the smallest totally tamely ramified extension of F_v over which chi_v becomes unramified. Let zeta be a primitive #k^× root of unity and N_0 = Q(zeta, sqrt(1-4l)); l is unramified in N_0 and every prime of N_0 above l has residue field isomorphic to k; fix lambda_0 | l and O_{N_0}/lambda_0 ≅ k. For v | l put beta_v = zeta^{b_v} ((1+sqrt(1-4l))/2)^{[k(v):F_l]} with beta_v ≡ chi_v(phi_v) mod lambda_0 for a Frobenius lift phi_v in G_{F~_v}, and let chi~_v: W_{F_v} -> N_0^× be the unique character which, if chi_v^2 ≠ 1, sends phi_v to beta_v and is the Teichmüller lift of chi_v on inertia, and, if chi_v^2 = 1, is the Teichmüller lift of chi_v. nodes.title: Taylor Lemma 1.1: a character of a CM quadratic extension with prescribed local reductions and prescribed determinant of its induction
nodes.statement: Let p be a rational prime, O the integers of a finite extension of Q_p with residue field F. Let K be totally real and L/K a totally imaginary quadratic extension in which every place of K above p splits. Let S be a finite set of finite places of K which split in L and contain all places above p, and S_L a set of places of L containing exactly one place above each element of S. Let phi: G_K -> O^× be continuous, sending every complex conjugation to -1 and of the form epsilon_p^n times a finite-order character for some n in Z. For each x in S_L let psi-bar_x: G_{L_x} -> F^× be continuous. Then there are a finite extension of Frac(O), with integers O' and residue field k', and a continuous character psi: G_L -> (O')^× such that for all x in S_L, psi|G_{L_x} is finitely ramified and reduces to psi-bar_x, and det Ind_{G_L}^{G_K} psi = phi.
hypotheses: every place of K above p splits in L; every place of S splits in L; S contains the places above p
phi odd (every complex conjugation to -1) and a power of epsilon_p times a finite-order character
the final step imports 'lemma 2.1 of [Ta2]' (Taylor, On icosahedral Artin representations II, Amer. J. Math. 125 (2003)), which the source calls presumably well known; [Ta2] is not in the library
proofSteps: Choose psi_0 with epsilon_p^{-1} det Ind psi_0 of finite order and psi_0|I_x of finite order for x in S_L; seeking psi = psi_0^n psi' reduces to n = 0; one may assume S_L generates the class group of L.

By class field theory, let psi_x: L_x^× -> O^× correspond to the Teichmüller lift of psi-bar_x and phi' the idele character of K attached to phi times the quadratic character of L/K; one must find psi: A_L^×/L^× -> (O')^× restricting to phi' on A_K^× and to psi_x on L_x^× for x in S_L.

With T the finite places outside S where phi' ramifies and chosen extensions psi_x of phi'|O_{K,x}^× to O_{L,x}^× for x in T, define psi_0 on (prod_{x in S} L_x^× × prod_{x in T} O_{L,x}^×)/K_S^×; it suffices to extend to a character of the product with prod_{y not in S∪T} (O_{L,y}^×/O_{K,y}^×) modulo L_S^×, i.e. to find a continuous character on that last product agreeing with psi_0 on L_S^×/K_S^×.

As psi_0 has finite order it suffices that every finite-index subgroup of L_S^×/K_S^× contains the preimage of an open subgroup of prod_{y not in S∪T} O_{L,y}^×/O_{K,y}^×; the commutative diagram with the map c-1 and finite generation of L_S^× reduce this to: for every n, (L_S^×)^n contains the preimage of an open subgroup of prod O_{L,y}^× -- the imported statement from [Ta2], Lemma 2.1.

nodes.title: M-HBAVs, ordered invertible O_M-modules, and the j(1)-Weil pairing
nodes.statement: For a totally real field M, an ordered invertible O_M-module is an invertible O_M-module X with a choice of connected component X_x^+ of (X ⊗ M_x) - {0} for each infinite place x of M; the standard one O_M^+ is (O_M, {(M_x^×)^0}). An M-HBAV over a field K is a triple (A, i, j) with A/K an abelian variety of dimension [M:Q], i: O_M -> End(A/K), and j: O_M^+ -> P(A, i) an isomorphism of ordered invertible O_M-modules, where P(A, i) is the invertible O_M-module of symmetric homomorphisms (A, i) -> (A^∨, i^∨) ordered by the component containing the class of a polarisation (Rapoport, section 1). Notation (preprint pp. 5-6): for a finite-index O_M-submodule X of a free O_M-module, A ⊗_{O_M} X is defined and (A ⊗ X)[a] = A[a] ⊗ X; if mu: A -> A^∨ is a polarisation inducing c on M and f: X -> Hom(X, Z) is c-semilinear with f(x)(x) totally strictly positive for x ≠ 0, then mu ⊗ f is a polarisation of A ⊗ X. For an ideal lambda prime to char K, rho-bar_{A,lambda} is the action on A[lambda](K^ac); the j(1)-Weil pairing on A[lambda] is the Weil pairing of the polarisation j(1).
hypotheses: M totally real (in Taylor 2002, M is the maximal totally real subfield of the CM field N)
the definition of P(A, i) and its ordering is imported from Rapoport, Compactifications de l'espace de modules de Hilbert-Blumenthal, Compositio 36 (1978), section 1 (not in the library)

nodes.title: The fine moduli space X/F of M-HBAVs with lambda- and wp-level structures matching prescribed alternating pairings
nodes.statement: Let V_lambda/F be the two-dimensional (O_M/lambda)-vector space scheme attached to rho-bar and fix an alternating isomorphism a_lambda of V_lambda with its Cartier dual; let V_wp be the two-dimensional (O_M/wp)-vector space scheme attached to Ind_{G_L}^{G_F} psi-bar and fix an alternating isomorphism a_wp of V_wp with its Cartier dual. nodes.statement: Let v be an unramified place of F above l and x a place of E above v. Suppose chi_v^2|I_v = epsilon^n|I_v for some integer n with 0 <= n < l - 1, and suppose that n ≠ 1 if rho-bar|G_v is semisimple. From the action on T_wp A, either A has multiplicative reduction over E_x (then chi_1 is unramified and the result is clear) or good reduction over E_x(zeta_l).

In the good reduction case, over W(k(x)^ac)[zeta_l] the only simple subquotients of the finite flat group scheme A[lambda] are Z/lZ and mu_l, and there are no nontrivial extensions of Z/lZ by Z/lZ nor of mu_l by mu_l; with the connected-étale sequence and dim Lie(A[lambda] × F_l^ac) = [O_N/lambda : F_l] this gives 0 -> mu_l^[O_N/lambda:F_l] -> A[lambda] -> (Z/lZ)^[O_N/lambda:F_l] -> 0, so A has ordinary reduction; done if rho-bar|G_v is not semisimple.

nodes.title: Taylor Theorem 1.6 (with the 2006 corrected proof) and Corollary 1.7: potential modularity of residual representations
nodes.statement: (Theorem 1.6) Let l be an odd prime, k/F_l finite, F totally real and rho-bar: G_F -> GL_2(k) continuous irreducible with rho-bar|G_v ~ (epsilon chi_v^{-1}, *; 0, chi_v) for every v | l and det rho-bar(c) = -1 for every complex conjugation c. Then there are a finite Galois totally real extension E/F in which every prime of F above l splits completely, a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation pi of GL_2(A_E) and a place lambda' of its field of coefficients above l with rho-bar_{pi,lambda'} ~ rho-bar|G_E. Moreover E, pi, lambda' may be chosen so that for every unramified prime x of E above l with chi_x^2|I_x = epsilon^n|I_x and rho-bar(I_x) not consisting of scalar matrices, rho_{pi,lambda'}|G_x ~ (epsilon (chi'_x)^{-1}, *; 0, chi'_x) with chi'_x a tamely ramified lift of chi_x. (Proposition 1) If (a) for l in S - {p, ∞}, R_{X,l} is a complete intersection, flat over Z_p, of relative dimension h^0(G_l, Ad_X) - Delta_l, and (b) R_{X,p} is a complete intersection, flat over Z_p, of relative dimension h^0(G_p, Ad_X) + 1 + d - Delta_p, then with Delta = sum Delta_l, R_X ≅ O[[x_1, ..., x_{n+d}]]/(f_1, ..., f_{n+Delta}). With fixed determinant, Delta_p = 0 for finite or Selmer conditions at p except when rho|G_p is decomposable and flat, handled by (Lemma 1) for rho|G_p ≅ epsilon-bar ⊕ 1 with flat lifts of determinant epsilon, R_{X^eta,p} ≅ W(k)[[X_1, X_2]]; Delta_l = 0 for l ∈ S - {p, ∞} when X_l allows no ramification, imposes no condition, is minimal at l (rho ramified as in Khare section 2), or is the Q-new condition at l ∈ Q. (Corollary 1) R_∅ and R_Q^{alpha-new} have presentations O[[x_1..x_n]]/(f_1..f_m) with m <= n. (Lemma 2) A CNL O-algebra finite as an O-module with such a presentation, m <= n, is a complete intersection, finite flat over O. (Corollary 2) If R_Q is finite over O then R_∅ is a complete intersection finite flat over O (using R_Q -> R_∅ surjective). (Theorem 1) If R_Q -> T_Q is an isomorphism of finite flat W(k)-algebras for some auxiliary Q, then R_∅ -> T_∅ is an isomorphism.

proofSteps: Proposition 1: present each R_{X,l} (l ∈ S' = S ∪ S_aux ∪ {p}) with n_l generators and j_l relations, where n_l = j_l + h^0(G_l, Ad_X) - Delta_l (+ 1 + d at p); [1] Theorem 5.6 gives R_X ≅ O[[x_1..x_{n+d}]]/J with J generated by at most j = sum j_l elements; [1] Lemma 5.5(ii) for odd rho gives n + d = d - Delta + sum j_l, so n + Delta = j.

Lemma 1: flat lifts of determinant epsilon are reducible (Conrad Theorem 1.8(ii)), the tangent space has dimension 2 (Conrad Lemma 3.4) so R = W(k)[[X_1, X_2]]/I; if I ≠ 0, the map (phi, psi) from flat W(k)-points to m × U is surjective with infinite fibres of h, contradicting finiteness of fibres of h on the affinoid X_f; so I = 0.

Lemma 2: A = O[[x_1..x_n]] is regular local of dimension n + 1; R/(pi) finite forces (pi, f_1..f_m) to have height n + 1, so m = n; by Matsumura Theorem 17.4, pi, f_1, ..., f_n is a regular sequence; hence R is a complete intersection and pi is a nonzerodivisor, so R is flat over O.

Theorem 1: all four rings of the square R_Q -> T_Q, R_∅ -> T_∅ are finite flat over W(k); after ⊗ K the Hecke algebras become products of copies of K-bar indexed by eigenforms M_Q, M_∅; a form in M_Q - M_∅ arising from R_∅ would be unramified at the primes of Q, forcing its conductor prime to Q by Carayol, a contradiction.

nodes.title: Prescribed-type strengthening used by the modern route: Gee Corollary 3.1.7 and Snowden Theorem 7.2.1 (p odd)
nodes.statement: (Gee, Corollary 3.1.7) Let p > 2, F totally real, S a finite set of places containing those above p and ∞, Σ ⊂ S its finite places, rho-bar: G_{F,S} -> GL_2(F) continuous with rho-bar|G_{F(zeta_p)} absolutely irreducible and rho-bar modular (and [F(zeta_5):F] ≠ 2 if p = 5 with projective image PGL_2(F_5)); psi = chi epsilon with chi of finite order; for v ∈ Σ Galois types tau_v with det tau_v = chi|I_{F_v}. If every local ring R_{v,psi,tau_v} is nonzero and hypothesis (ord) holds (rho-bar ≅ rho-bar_f for a parallel weight 2 Hilbert form f potentially ordinary exactly where the chosen components are ordinary and not special above p), then there is a modular lift of rho-bar, potentially Barsotti-Tate above p, unramified outside S, of type tau_v at every v ∈ Σ, lying on chosen components. (Snowden, Theorem 7.2.1) Let F be totally real, p odd, rho-bar: G_F -> GL_2(F_p-bar) odd with (A1) rho-bar|G_{F(zeta_p)} absolutely irreducible and (A2) [F(zeta_5):F] = 4 if p = 5 and the projective image is PGL_2(F_5). For a lifting problem P = (Σ, psi, t, {tau_v}) (Σ containing the ramification of rho-bar and the places above p, psi of finite order with det rho-bar = psi-bar chi_p, a definite type function t: A, B or C above p and AB or C away from p, inertial types tau_v), P has only finitely many solutions (weight two lifts with determinant psi chi_p, unramified outside Σ, of type t(v) and inertial type tau_v), and a solution exists if and only if a local solution exists.
hypotheses: p odd in both (Snowden does not consider p = 2; Gee's section 3 assumes p > 2)
